newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Banco Totta rallies but upside capped.
newsitem.headline: Banco Totta rallies but upside capped.

text.p: Portugal's Banco Totta & Acores, whose stock crashed this week on worse than expected profits, rallied strongly on Friday but analysts said further upside gains were limited.
Totta was gaining 120 escudos at 2,570 after being re-admitted to trade following its suspension before the start of trade on Friday.

Trade had been halted after newspaper reports -- subsequently denied -- that the Champalimaud group was planning to merge Totta with sister bank Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor . It controls both financial institutions.
"Banco Totta can recover but not too much further. The fundamental questions still remain," said Pedro Assuncao of Central Investimentos.
Analysts said that the stock could aim for somewhere between 2,600 and 2,700 escudos in coming sessions but that it would not reach levels about 3,000 escudos seen before the crash.

The slump was triggered by a group announcement that profit for 1996 was only some 15 billion escudos, down from 17.2 billion in 1995 and significantly below the 18 to 19 billion that many analysts had been looking for.

But analysts said that the selling had probably been overdone and that this rebound effect together with the fact the group could eventually come up with slightly higher figures could help the stock to recover some ground.
"It (the stock) was getting down to around its book value," said one Lisbon analyst who asked not to be named.

Analysts said that the bank could eventually announce that last year's profit was in fact around 16-16.5 billion escudos, still below levels originally expected, but better than the initial announcement.
The dividend, which had been announced at 135 escudos, far below the 180-190 escudos predicted, would almost certainly turn out to be higher, too, they said.
Businessman Antonio Champalimaud, who heads the group that controls the two banks, had already made clear his dissatisfaction with the level of the payout.

His son, Luis, who combines the chairmanship of Banco Totta and Sotto Mayor, indicated that the numbers could indeed improve with a statement on Thursday night saying that 15 billion escudos was a minimum profit level.
Portugal's Financial Markets Committee allowed trading in both banks to resume after the group denied that it planned to merge Banco Totta into Sotto Mayor.
But analysts said that the statements by the group did nothing to answer the main question in investors' minds -- what would be the future of the two banks within the group?
"Until it is answered, Banco Totta will continue at a considerable discount to the market," said one Lisbon analyst.
